verdict.rationale: Meilisearch's own docs say that once an embedder is configured, the engine automatically generates vector embeddings for every document, so the developer does not compute or manage them. Hybrid and semantic search use those embeddings at query time. However, the pack never explicitly documents query-side vectorization or names which built-in or managed embedder providers are available, so story coverage is incomplete. missing for 10: explicit documentation that queries are auto-embedded, details of which built-in/managed embedder sources are supported, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can use built-in or managed embedders so documents and queries are vectorized without running my own embedding pipeline

citations.quote: When you configure an embedder, Meilisearch automatically generates vector embeddings for every document in your index. You don't need to compute or manage embeddings yourself.
Hybrid search combines two search strategies: full-text search (matching keywords) and semantic search (matching meaning).
It stores your documents and embeddings, then exposes them through fast full-text search, semantic search, and conversational interfaces, all from a single API.
